clue.text: One may to be orally examined in it

definitions.text: One may to be orally examined in it

parts.words: One may to be orally examined in it
parts.note: an oral examination sounds academic, like a viva, but here it is a look inside the mouth by a tooth doctor, in the seat the patient sits in

explanation.surface: A candidate sits in some seat to face a spoken exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orally examined' suggests a viva voce exam; read literally, it is having your mouth inspected.
explanation.definitionFit: Patients sit in this reclining seat while their teeth and gums are inspected.

clue.text: Change of fee as required to take off the pressure

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of the words that follow it

explanation.surface: A fee is adjusted as needed to relieve financial strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges the letters of 'of fee as'; 'required to' just links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax or slacken effort is to reduce strain.

clue.text: Common habits?

parts.note: habits are clothes, as a monk's habit is, and 'common' means an informal, slangy word for them

explanation.surface: A question about what ordinary people routinely do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habits' looks like routines; it means garments, and 'common' asks for the colloquial word.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang word for clothing, used informally rather than in polite speech.

clue.text: Bashful rugby player shows character

parts.note: bashful means shy
a lock is a second-row forward in rugby

explanation.surface: A timid rugby forward reveals his true nature.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'character' is a figure in a play: the moneylender in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's moneylender in The Merchant of Venice is a famous stage figure.

clue.text: Young players may be found in this bunker

definitions.text: Young players may be found in this bunker

parts.words: Young players may be found in this bunker
parts.note: a bunker on a golf course is a sand trap, so young golfers seem meant, but the players are small children playing in sand

explanation.surface: Junior golfers end up stuck in a sand trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunker' and 'players' suggest golf; the place is a child's sand-filled play area.
explanation.definitionFit: A play area filled with sand, where small children dig and build.

clue.text: He gets a little publicity as a school principal

parts.note: taken as written
an ad is a short advertisement, a small piece of publicity

explanation.surface: A headteacher gets a brief mention in the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: The teacher in charge of a British school is called by this short title.

clue.text: You might be if a plan goes wrong

definitions.text: You might be if a plan goes wrong

indicators.note: a plan that goes wrong falls apart, so the letters of 'if a plan' are jumbled

explanation.surface: You would be flustered when a scheme collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the anagram of 'if a plan' at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Being agitated and panicky is the natural state when a scheme fails.

clue.text: He has nothing new to offer

definitions.text: He has nothing new to offer

parts.words: He has nothing new to offer
parts.note: it sounds like criticism of a dull person, but it describes a trader whose stock is entirely old furniture and curios

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about someone with no fresh ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a put-down; literally, all the goods for sale are old.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of old furniture and collectable objects has only aged stock.

clue.text: Showing signs of fight?

parts.note: signs of fight sounds like aggression or spirit, but it means marks left on the body by combat

explanation.surface: Someone appears ready for a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signs of fight' looks like a fighting mood; it means wounds from past combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked with wounds from war or conflict.

clue.text: Flowers, say, gone astray

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters of 'say gone' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bouquet, so to speak, has wandered off.
explanation.definitionFit: A small posy or bunch of blooms.

clue.text: Falls for a redhead once more on the rebound

indicators.note: a ball on the rebound comes back the way it went, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of red is R
once more means again

explanation.surface: Someone falls for a red-haired woman again after a break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rebound' turns A + R + AGAIN backwards. 'Falls' looks like a verb but is the definition: the waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfall on the US-Canadian border.

clue.text: Trickster admitting his image?

parts.note: a trickster owning up to his trade says it in the first person, giving I
a con, short for con man, is a swindler

explanation.surface: A conman confesses to having a picture of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The trickster admitting what he does would say 'I con'.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious picture or symbol, a likeness venerated in Orthodox churches.

clue.text: Car to handle well going round a bend

indicators.note: going round means the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: to cope is to manage or handle a situation
a U-bend is a U-shaped bend, so U stands for a bend

explanation.surface: A car that corners nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-door motor with a fixed roof and sloping back.

clue.text: Plan shows parking place

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
a lot is a site or patch of land

explanation.surface: A scheme reveals a spot for leaving the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme or secret intrigue.

clue.text: Sum for small child, a learner

parts.note: a tot is a toddler
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: Arithmetic for a little kid just learning.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole amount obtained by adding.

clue.text: Scene of a towering row!

parts.note: a towering row sounds like a huge argument; it is the din of tongues at the biblical tower in Genesis

explanation.surface: Where a tremendous quarrel broke out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Towering row' suggests a massive argument; the row is the confusion of languages at the biblical tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical city whose tower led to the confusion of languages, so a byword for noisy confusion.

clue.text: Give the sack to a priest, outcome of fun and beat music?

definitions.text: Give the sack to a priest

indicators.note: the outcome of something is what it is turned into, so the letters of fun are reworked

parts.note: rock is music with a strong beat

explanation.surface: A vicar is sacked after a jolly night of rock and roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outcome of' rearranges FUN into UNF.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip a cleric of clerical status, defrocking him.

clue.text: Long walk pirates ordered

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new order, so the letters of pirates are rearranged

explanation.surface: Buccaneers are commanded to make a long march.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiring, trudging trek.

clue.text: Independent air of Ned's cat, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible version, so the letters of Ned's cat are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ned's cat has an aloof manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' looks like an attitude; it is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A separate melody sung or played above the main tune.

clue.text: Product of a fruitful harem?

parts.note: a harem's member is a sultan's wife, and the same word names a dried grape, so 'fruitful' plays both ways

explanation.surface: Asking what offspring a fertile harem yields.
explanation.walkthrough: A sultan's wife and a raisin share one name; 'fruitful' hints at the dried fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a sultan's wife and a seedless dried grape.

clue.text: Sauce label for company

parts.note: a tab is a small tag or label
for can mean as, in the sense of 'serving as'

explanation.surface: A sauce bottle's label is made for a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chilli pepper condiment from Louisiana.

clue.text: Woman will get the bill for coat

parts.note: she refers to a woman
'll is the short form of will
ac or a/c is an abbreviation for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A woman will be invoiced for a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coat' is a layer of varnish, not a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A resin varnish applied as a layer to wood.

clue.text: Clients' letters bashed out — from this?

definitions.text: Clients' letters bashed out — from this?

indicators.note: letters bashed out are beaten into a new shape, so the letters of Clients are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive apostrophe gives no letter

explanation.surface: Customers' correspondence is typed up quickly from a template.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a cut-out sheet through which letters are painted.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-out template through which ink or paint marks out lettering.

clue.text: Incorrect in angle?

indicators.note: incorrect means not right, so the letters of 'in angle' are wrongly ordered and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether something is wrongly angled.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well: something out of true is tilted.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilting away from the vertical, not standing true.

clue.text: Declines to set sail

indicators.note: set can mean arranged, so the letters of sail are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to go sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: Weakens or falls sick, as health declines.

clue.text: Instruments of love in high orders

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: OBEs are awards in the Order of the British Empire
love is nil in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Musical instruments of love feature in honours lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Double-reed woodwinds.

clue.text: Place where cub may be left warm and dry

parts.note: to air laundry is to warm and dry it, as in an airing cupboard

explanation.surface: A young animal's den is left warm and dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild animal's den, where young are reared.

clue.text: Between-maid seeking new position

indicators.note: a maid seeking a new position wants a new job; here her letters shift to new places

explanation.surface: A between-maid looks for another job.
explanation.walkthrough: A between-maid was a junior servant; 'Between' is the definition, split off by the hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: Means in the middle of or among.

clue.text: Took off commercial about keep-fit exercises

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: Someone left an advert about fitness classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took off' looks like departed; it means mimicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimicked or imitated someone.

clue.text: The scholar takes ages with complicated sum

parts.note: eras are ages

indicators.note: complicated means tangled, so the letters of sum are mixed up

explanation.surface: An academic takes a long time over a tricky calculation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch Renaissance humanist, the best-known scholar of his age.

clue.text: Prisoner's madly active, but quiet inside

definitions.note: read as 'prisoner is', a noun naming the person held

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other
madly signals a crazy rearrangement of active

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A jailbird is wildly busy yet keeps calm within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madly' rearranges ACTIVE into CATIVE, and 'inside' puts P within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person taken and held, a captured detainee.

clue.text: Cynical urge one may get at a picnic

definitions.text: one may get at a picnic

parts.note: hard-boiled means tough and cynical
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: A jaded impulse strikes someone on an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelled food cooked firm, a standard cold item packed for outdoor meals.
